newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends up on Tokyo stock tumble.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends up on Tokyo stock tumble.

text.p: The key September Euroyen futures contract closed substantially higher on TIFFE on Thursday due to the Tokyo stock market's tumble and hedge buying by foreign accounts, traders said.
Tokyo's Nikkei closed at the lowest level this year, tumbling 2.60 percent to 19,570.67 points.
The steep stock fall reignited expectations that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will continue its ultra easy money policy.
Some said other foreign accounts were active sellers of Nikkei index futures on SIMEX and buyers of TIFFE's Euroyen.
The Japan premium -- the extra cost Japanese banks are charged when raising funds in the Euro interbank market -- narrowed slightly, but is still at a high level.
Major Japanese city banks were paying a premium of about 34 basis points (BPS) over the prevailing one-month Eurodollar deposit rate of 5.59375 percent.
Traders said that some local banks are raising yen funds and converting them into dollars in the currency forward market to meet their dollar needs.
Some said such banks' demands for yen is underpinning short-term interest rates.
The key three-month certificate of deposit was at 0.51 percent, at which approximately 90 billion yen was traded.
The BOJ conducted a reserve neutral operation at its regular operation time via injecting 500 billion yen into the market which had projected shortfall of 510 billion yen.
